newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina bill would end tax for those over 65.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina bill would end tax for those over 65.

text.p: The South Carolina Senate overwhelmingly approved a proposal to eliminate income taxes for senior citizens beginning in 1998, the State newspaper reported Wednesday.
The proposal passed 40-2 on Tuesday in the Democrat-majority Senate.
Although it was proposed by Republican Gov. David Beasley, it is expected to run into trouble in the Republican-ruled House, where a budget committee has already rejected the cut as too costly.
Under the plan, South Carolina residents over 65 would see their income tax deductions rise to $11,500 from $10,000 in 1997. They would be totally exempt from state income taxes in 1998.
Social Security income is exempt from state income taxes, so many of the state's 440,000 senior citizens already have incomes below the $10,000 taxable threshhold.
About 145,000 senior citizens paid state income taxes last year on $834 million of non-Social Security income.
About 12 percent of South Carolina residents are over 65, and the figure is projected to rise to 20 percent, or one million residents, by 2025.
Sen. Verne Smith, D-Greenville, and Sen. Robert Waldrep, R-Anderson, were the only two senators to vote against the tax break.
Smith, 72, said it would put a strain on working families and send retirees the message, "Come on down here, you rich Yankees, and let our hard-working people pay you're way."
